definition: Techniques for combining the weights of multiple trained models (often fine-tuned variants of the same base model) into a single model without additional training.
details: Model merging methods, such as weight averaging or task-vector arithmetic, can combine capabilities from multiple specialized fine-tunes into one model at little to no additional training cost.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Model Merging.
